core_obligations: Reduce to Cech cohomology (proof lines 9288-9292): the vanishing of the lemma follows from the Cech-to-derived comparison once all higher Cech cohomology groups of g^{-1}I with respect to an arbitrary covering U = {U_i -> U} of C are shown to vanish.

Compare the Cech complexes (proof lines 9293-9302): since u is continuous and cocontinuous, the family u(U) is a covering of D and u preserves the fibre products U_{i_0} x_U ... x_U U_{i_n}, so the Cech complex of U with coefficients in g^{-1}I equals the Cech complex of u(U) with coefficients in I, because g^{-1} = u^p.

Conclude (proof lines 9303-9307): the Cech cohomology groups of the injective module I with respect to the covering u(U) vanish by the injectivity lemma, so the groups on the left vanish for all p > 0 and all U.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the cohomology vanishing to the vanishing of all higher Cech groups of coverings.
Identify the Cech complex of a covering with that of its image covering, using cocontinuity and the fibre-product compatibility.
Apply the vanishing of the Cech cohomology of an injective module.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the pullback of an injective module along a continuous cocontinuous functor of sites has vanishing higher cohomology on the objects of the source site (statement lines 9277-9285). The proof (proof lines 9287-9307) reduces to Cech cohomology, identifies the Cech complex of a covering with that of its image under u using cocontinuity and the compatibility of u with fibre products, and invokes the vanishing of Cech cohomology for injective modules. H2: one reduction plus one identification of complexes, written out.
